# 1 Samuel Chapter 19 — Disagreement Log
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **Book:** 1 Samuel | **Chapter:** 19

---

### Verse 1
- **EMET:** "And-Saul-spoke to Jonathan his-son and-to all his-servants to-put-David-to-death. And-Jonathan, son of-Saul, delighted in-David exceedingly."
- **LOGOS:** "And Saul spoke to Jonathan his son and to all his servants about killing David. But Jonathan, Saul's son, delighted greatly in David."
- **PNEUMA:** "Saul told his son Jonathan and all his servants to kill David. But Jonathan, Saul's son, was deeply devoted to David."
- **Resolution:** SOPHIA follows the LOGOS rendering as the formal-equivalence baseline, noting PNEUMA's dynamic phrasing as a valid alternative reading.
### Verse 12
- **EMET:** "And-Michal-let-David-down through the-window, and-he-went and-fled and-escaped."
- **LOGOS:** "So Michal let David down through the window, and he went and fled and escaped."
- **PNEUMA:** "So Michal lowered David through a window, and he fled and escaped."
- **Resolution:** SOPHIA follows the LOGOS rendering as the formal-equivalence baseline, noting PNEUMA's dynamic phrasing as a valid alternative reading.
### Verse 15
- **EMET:** "And-Saul-sent the-messengers to-see David, saying, "Bring-him-up to-me in-the-bed, to-put-him-to-death.""
- **LOGOS:** "Then Saul sent the messengers to see David, saying, "Bring him up to me in the bed, that I may kill him.""
- **PNEUMA:** "Saul sent the men back to see David, telling them, "Bring him up to me on his bed so I can kill him.""
- **Resolution:** SOPHIA follows the LOGOS rendering as the formal-equivalence baseline, noting PNEUMA's dynamic phrasing as a valid alternative reading.
### Verse 16
- **EMET:** "And-the-messengers-came, and-behold, the-teraphim [was] on the-bed, and-the-quilt of-goats' [hair] at-its-head."
- **LOGOS:** "And when the messengers came in, behold, the household idol was on the bed, with the quilt of goats' hair at its head."
- **PNEUMA:** "When the men entered, there was the idol on the bed with the goat's hair at its head."
- **Resolution:** SOPHIA follows the LOGOS rendering as the formal-equivalence baseline, noting PNEUMA's dynamic phrasing as a valid alternative reading.

— SOPHIA
